evidence.exact_quote: Native desktop targets Windows, Linux, and macOS through the Slint Winit backend. The compiled renderer availability order is Winit + Skia, Winit + FemtoVG-wgpu, then Winit software renderer. Runtime selection resolves in this order: `SLINT_BACKEND` explicit override, persisted renderer preference, compiled Skia default, FemtoVG-wgpu fallback, and software emergency fallback. `SLINT_BACKEND` remains valid for debugging, CI, and operator override, but persisted preferences must not silently override an explicit environment override. Startup diagnostics record the requested backend, effective backend, fallback reason, platform, GPU/driver summary when available, and whether the fallback was operator-selected or automatic.

items.impact: Implementers have a deterministic native renderer precedence and an inspectable fallback record, reducing platform-specific selection drift.
items.statement: The native renderer contract fixes both precedence and required startup diagnostics, including the rule that persisted preference cannot override an explicit environment selection.
items.title: Native renderer selection is deterministic and observable

evidence.exact_quote: The web GUI may use OS-owned capabilities only through a trusted local Puppet Master daemon. The daemon boundary requires authenticated local origin or pairing, origin and CSRF protection, capability probing before feature enablement, explicit permission requests for sensitive operations, receipt/audit events for granted or denied actions, redaction before display or persistence, degraded reasons when the daemon is absent or narrowed, and deterministic agent-test hooks for fixture mode and browser automation. The web GUI consumes daemon capability receipts; it does not infer authority from localhost reachability alone.

items.impact: A daemon disconnect, permission revocation, or capability narrowing during a sensitive operation can be handled differently by different builders, risking duplicate mutation, an indeterminate result, or misleading success state.
items.statement: The daemon boundary specifies admission checks and receipts but not the in-flight state machine for daemon loss, permission revocation, re-pairing, cancellation, outcome reconciliation, or retry idempotency.
items.title: Trusted-daemon authority has no in-flight revocation contract

evidence.exact_quote: Projection-backed surfaces use `freshness_state` values `current`, `refreshing`, `stale`, `degraded`, and `unavailable`; `/current` projections may allow normal read/write interaction, while `stale` or `/degraded` surfaces narrow mutation-bearing actions, disable them, or require direct canonical/current revalidation before execution.

items.impact: The same stale or degraded condition can yield hidden, disabled, narrowed, or revalidated mutations depending on implementation choice, making authority and recovery behavior inconsistent across surfaces.
items.statement: The projection grammar enumerates several allowed responses to stale or degraded data but does not bind action classes or reason codes to one required gate behavior and oracle.
items.title: Projection trust does not deterministically select an action gate

evidence.exact_quote: Production GUI surfaces use bundled local SVG assets referenced by stable `icon_id`. The production UI must not use emoji, emoji-like pictographs, Dingbat-style pseudo-icons, or Unicode pictographs as controls, badges, status indicators, or decorative substitutes for icons. Concept glyphs from PMConcept or other source-lineage artifacts map only to approved `icon_id` entries before promotion.

The local SVG manifest includes `icon_id`, file path, semantic label, theme behavior, size slots, accessible label, fallback text, and any state-variant mapping. Icons are never the sole carrier of state: every icon-only control has an accessible label, tooltip or equivalent label projection, keyboard/focus behavior, and nearby or programmatic state text. Network/CDN icon fonts or remote SVG/icon imports are forbidden for production GUI source.

items.impact: The icon source, identity, fallback, state redundancy, and accessibility obligations are fixed before implementation.
items.statement: Production iconography is locally bundled SVG-only, forbids emoji and remote icon sources, and requires labels, keyboard behavior, and non-icon state text.
items.title: SVG-only no-emoji UI contract is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Approve And Build is the only ordinary final planning approval-to-PlanCompileRun launch authority. It dispatches `cmd.planning_wizard.approve_and_build`, carries the displayed final-review CAS/currentness inputs, writes `approval_cas_receipt`, publishes `PlanApproved`, creates or binds exactly one `PlanCompileRun` synchronously, and opens Orchestrator Plan Compile in pending-launch or durable-run state. No `START`, `BUILD`, or `Approve & Continue` control may create a second ordinary launch from the same approval inputs. Post-approval controls use scoped labels such as `Open Plan Compile`, `Open Build`, `Pause`, `Resume`, `Retry`, or `Approve Step` only when their command, disabled reason, receipt effect, and stale-projection behavior are defined.

items.impact: Ordinary final approval has a single authority, currentness input, receipt, event, synchronous run binding, and explicit duplicate-launch prohibition.
items.statement: The Planning Wizard final approval path explicitly binds approval CAS evidence to exactly one PlanCompileRun and forbids alternate ordinary launch controls.
items.title: Approve And Build has explicit single-launch authority

evidence.exact_quote: - Docker/Hosts is reachable as a routed primary-content Slint page/lab from Docker Manager and cross-surface links.
- docker_manager remains the Activity Bar side-panel owner and command namespace.

items.impact: The expanded page can be reached by all intended consumers without creating a competing shell owner or activity slot.
items.statement: F3-410 defines Docker/Hosts as a routed primary-content Slint lab while retaining Docker Manager as operational, command-namespace, and Activity Bar ownership.
items.title: Docker/Hosts routed lab preserves Docker Manager ownership

evidence.exact_quote: `supported_with_limits`, `degraded`, `unsupported`, `disabled_until_approval`, and `blocked`; instance/session
states are `not_created`, `preflight_required`, `preflighting`, `preflight_passed`, `provisioning`, `starting`,
- The component tree and lifecycle state matrix above are represented in the native Slint page model before coding begins.

items.impact: Provision, stop, cleanup, retain, retry, and approval actions can diverge on legal predecessor states, duplicate-command handling, concurrent requests, and post-crash reconciliation even though the same state names are rendered.
items.statement: F3-410 enumerates rich profile, runtime-family, instance, session, and access states but supplies no transition graph, command preconditions, idempotency key, race policy, or recovery-to-terminal-state oracle.
items.title: Docker/Hosts state lists are not a lifecycle state machine

evidence.exact_quote: - Tests cover Docker Manager opening Docker/Hosts as primary content, every toolbar/card action mapping to a registered command, stale projections disabling lifecycle mutation, low-confidence Open App disabling, blocked cards showing allowed actions, and mobile/tablet/desktop layouts preserving critical blockers.

items.impact: Builders can choose incompatible breakpoints, collapse priorities, and blocker-preservation mechanisms while still claiming that mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts preserve critical blockers.
items.statement: The responsive acceptance sentence names three form-factor classes but defines no viewport fixtures, minimum visible blocker fields, overflow behavior, keyboard order, or screenshot/semantic oracle.
items.title: Docker/Hosts responsive acceptance is not falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: Provider settings and run controls must present concrete provider/account/model rows from the Provider -> models catalog. Selectors are account-profile driven, show provider family grouping only as display metadata, expose thinking effort as requested intent where applicable, and disclose effective effort outcomes as honored, skipped, clamped, unsupported, or partially supported. Disabled, capability-gated, unverified, separate-profile, source-lineage-only, and retired/source-lineage provider states must be visible and actionable without implying generic provider failure.

items.impact: The GUI cannot flatten account-backed catalog rows, requested effort, effective outcome, or support-state reasons into a generic provider selector.
items.statement: F3-400 requires provider/account/model selectors to be driven by account profiles and to separate requested thinking effort from the effective honored, skipped, clamped, unsupported, or partial outcome.
items.title: Provider selector preserves account and effort truth

evidence.exact_quote: - Provider/model selectors are driven by provider entry, account profile, model row, and support-state data.
- Thinking effort UI distinguishes requested and effective outcomes.

items.impact: A selected account/model can be retired, gated, or reclassified between display and dispatch without a specified stale-selection state, revalidation outcome, preservation rule, or recovery path.
items.statement: F3-400 defines the selector inputs and labels but not how catalog revision, account removal, capability change, or an in-flight run invalidates a previously selected row.
items.title: Provider selection lacks catalog-change transition semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - GUI distinguishes media input, media output, and generated-media routes.
- Do not make the GUI the owner of media schema truth.

items.impact: The picker cannot infer generation from input support or promote incomplete provider rows, and route-specific schemas remain owned outside the GUI.
items.statement: F3-401 explicitly separates media input, media output, and generated-media support and forbids GUI ownership of capability schema truth.
items.title: Media capability dimensions and ownership are separated

evidence.exact_quote: - MiniMax Image-01 controls include route-specific parameters and expiry/partial-success disclosures.
- Do not hide expiry, partial success, provider account, or provenance caveats from generated-media results.

items.impact: For multi-output requests, builders can disagree about whether success is per artifact or per request, whether retries regenerate successful outputs, how charges and seeds are represented, and which receipts prove completion.
items.statement: F3-401 requires a partial-success disclosure but never defines result cardinality, per-artifact status, retry scope, duplicate prevention, billing/provenance treatment, or a terminal acceptance oracle.
items.title: Generated-media partial success has no outcome contract

evidence.exact_quote: - MiniMax Image-01 controls include route-specific parameters and expiry/partial-success disclosures.
- Do not hide expiry, partial success, provider account, or provenance caveats from generated-media results.

items.impact: Expired remote results can remain presented as usable, disappear without durable artifact recovery, leak signed URL material into persistence or exports, or produce inconsistent offline behavior.
items.statement: The disclosure requirement does not define whether generated URLs are imported before expiry, redacted, refreshed, persisted, removed, or reconciled after offline use and application restart.
items.title: Generated-media URL expiry lacks a data lifecycle

evidence.exact_quote: - **Project bar:** Instant project switching from title bar with full state preservation and reload
The title bar no longer owns primary project switching.

items.impact: Navigation, command routing, persistence, accessibility copy, and tests can implement either a title-bar-owned single-project model or a workspace-tab-owned multi-project model.
items.statement: The executive summary promises instant project switching from a Project bar in the title bar, while the canonical shell section explicitly removes primary project-switch ownership from the title bar.
items.title: Project-switch ownership contradicts itself within FinalGUISpec

evidence.exact_quote: | `Escape` | Close palette / panel / stop agent |

items.impact: The same key can dismiss transient UI, close a panel, or interrupt active work; focus bugs or nested overlays can therefore trigger an unintended destructive interruption or make interruption inaccessible.
items.statement: The shortcut table overloads Escape across three consequences without defining focus-stack precedence, confirmation, repeat-press behavior, agent-stop scope, or an acceptance test for nested surfaces.
items.title: Escape overload has no command-arbitration contract

evidence.exact_quote: Search is also the `search-owner` for the full indexing control surface: enable/disable index, rebuild/re-anchor, large-file threshold default 10 MB, generated-file index-exclusion patterns, follow-symlinks toggle, and visible indexed/stale/unindexed/fallback state. If the user turns OFF indexing while a build is in progress, PM cancels the builder with `CancellationToken`, removes partial generation state, and on `re-enable` starts a fresh build. Settings may persist global defaults, but Search exposes the project-scoped same-freshness and `/freshness/degradation` control and status copy users need before interpreting results.

items.impact: Disabling indexing has defined cancellation, partial-state cleanup, and clean re-enable behavior instead of leaving a resumable corrupt generation.
items.statement: The Search owner contract explicitly cancels an in-progress index build, removes partial generation state, and requires a fresh build after re-enable.
items.title: Index disable and recovery semantics are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Graph-heavy and stream-heavy surfaces have a `/table` or list equivalent with full keyboard and `/screen-reader` parity; `/graph` views are never the only path to the same information. Source Control History and Graph on monorepos, `/Graph/Worktrees`, GitHub Actions run lists and `/job/step` logs, Docker asset explorers with many `/containers/tags`, Kubernetes workload `/log/watch` views, and receipt/history panes define `initial_window`, `page_size`, `max_live_rows`, `max_in_memory_rows`, load-older behavior, `/filter-first` rules, and pause plus `/follow/search/jump-to-latest` behavior for streams/logs.

items.impact: Dense graph and stream surfaces cannot ship without keyboard/screen-reader-equivalent list access and explicit bounded-window behavior.
items.statement: Cross-surface scaling requires list or table parity for graphs and named window, memory, history, filtering, and stream-follow controls.
items.title: Graph accessibility and stream scale have explicit parity requirements

evidence.exact_quote: Per panel: **DOCKED** <-> **FLOATING**. Same Slint component is used inline when docked or as the root of a separate Slint `Window` when floating.
+--[close floating window]--> DOCKED (collapsed)

items.impact: Collapsed, hidden, visible, and docked states can be encoded ad hoc outside the declared enum, producing restore mismatches, impossible transitions, or a panel that is logically docked but has no defined visibility state.
items.statement: The declared per-panel state machine contains only DOCKED and FLOATING, while its close transition produces DOCKED (collapsed) without representing collapsed state in PanelDock or specifying visibility restoration transitions.
items.title: Panel state machine emits an unmodeled collapsed state

evidence.exact_quote: - **Shared data:** All panel data (chat messages, file tree) lives in Rust (e.g., `Arc<RwLock<...>>`). Exposed to Slint via properties/Models (e.g., `VecModel`). Both docked and floating instances bind to the same Rust-backed properties via `Rc<VecModel<T>>` and Slint's `ModelNotify` for automatic propagation

**Data sync:** Floating and docked instances share the same `Rc<VecModel<T>>` and scalar properties. When the Rust side replaces an entire model (e.g., project switch), it must update the shared `Rc` in-place rather than reassigning the pointer, so both windows stay synchronized.

items.impact: Queued updates from the old project can land after a project switch, docked and floating views can transiently disagree, and whole-model replacement can expose partially updated or misidentified rows.
items.statement: Shared model identity is required, but there is no project/revision token, event ordering rule, atomic replacement boundary, stale callback rejection, or docked/floating convergence oracle.
items.title: Multi-window shared models lack revision and race semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - The GUI MUST expose exactly three built-in theme choices: `Retro Dark`, `Retro Light`, and `Basic`.
- Retro Dark, Retro Light, Basic Light, Basic Dark (the four variants in §6.1-6.2)

items.impact: The selector, migration keys, title-bar threshold, persistence, help copy, and accessibility tests can expose either three family choices or four built-in choices.
items.statement: The theme selector contract mandates exactly three built-in choices with Basic as one family, but the extensibility section calls Basic Light and Basic Dark separate built-in themes and describes four built-in variants as selector entries.
items.title: Theme contract alternates between three and four built-in choices

evidence.exact_quote: **Custom theme file format:** Custom themes are defined as TOML files in `~/.puppet-master/themes/<name>.toml`. Each file specifies token overrides; any token not specified inherits from the base theme (Basic Dark or Basic Light, chosen by a `base` field).

**Custom font support:** Custom themes can reference font files placed in `~/.puppet-master/fonts/`. Font files (.ttf, .otf, .woff2) are loaded at startup. A theme TOML referencing a missing font falls back to the base theme's font and shows a warning toast.

items.impact: Hostile or accidentally extreme theme and font files can cause path escape, oversized resource use, parser/font-engine faults, unreadable UI, hot-reload churn, or persistence of an unrecoverable active theme.
items.statement: Custom TOML and font loading lacks path/symlink confinement, file and directory limits, parse time bounds, font sanitization policy, atomic hot-reload behavior, rollback after invalid active edits, and a safe-mode recovery route.
items.title: Custom themes and fonts lack an untrusted-input contract

evidence.exact_quote: - **Retro themes:** Prioritize aesthetic over strict WCAG AA compliance for accent colors (e.g., ACID_LIME on dark backgrounds may not meet 4.5:1)

- **Basic theme:** MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA for all text and interactive elements (4.5:1 minimum contrast for normal text, 3:1 for large text). Basic accent colors are muted specifically to meet this requirement

items.impact: Two default user-facing theme choices may render text or interactive state below required contrast, excluding low-vision users and making accessibility acceptance depend on choosing Basic.
items.statement: The specification deliberately exempts Retro themes from strict AA accent contrast while requiring AA only for Basic, leaving production built-in themes without a universal readable-text and interactive-state oracle.
items.title: Retro built-in themes explicitly permit contrast failure

evidence.exact_quote: Every disabled mutation affordance uses the shared `disabled-control` explanation model. Disabled controls expose a short inline reason, a hover/focus tooltip with the exact blocking condition, and the primary recovery CTA when one exists. Controls remain keyboard-focusable when that focus is needed for `/accessibility`, explanation, or recovery discovery.

items.impact: Disabled actions must remain explainable and recovery-discoverable to pointer and keyboard users rather than merely becoming inert or visually muted.
items.statement: The shared disabled-control contract requires inline cause, exact hover/focus explanation, recovery CTA when available, and keyboard focus where needed to discover the explanation.
items.title: Disabled mutation controls have a shared accessible explanation model

segments.summary: Reviewed the canonical prologue, concern and projection grammar, native and web renderer boundaries, trusted-daemon authority, SVG/no-emoji accessibility, testing readiness, and Planning Wizard approval authority. Strong contracts coexist with unresolved projection-gate and daemon in-flight lifecycle choices plus a later contradiction in project-switch ownership.

Reviewed F3-410 and F3-400 completely. Ownership, route reachability, provider/account/model truth, and effort disclosure are explicit, while Docker/Hosts lifecycle transitions and responsive oracles remain underdefined and provider catalog invalidation lacks a state transition contract.

Reviewed F3-401 media capability requirements and the first continuation through shell layout, navigation, Search, scaling, command palette, shortcuts, and detachable-panel declaration. Media schema ownership and search recovery are strong, but generated-result partial success and expiry are not operationally closed, project switching contradicts the prologue, and Escape arbitration is unsafe.

Reviewed the second continuation through terminal detachment, panel state and recovery, multi-window data flow, theme families and customization, accessibility, Orchestrator projection presentation, and disabled-control behavior. The panel enum omits its collapsed result, shared models lack revision ordering, theme count contradicts itself, custom assets lack an untrusted-input boundary, and Retro themes permit contrast failure; disabled controls are nevertheless well specified.
